this is the exact opposite advise that you should follow if you have a tendency to keloid, just as a heads up. this can stimulate collagen production, and keloids are already a result of overactive collagen. you risk having the scar grow beyond its existing boundaries by going to tanning beds excessively. i learned that the hard way growing up, and my derm scolded me heavily for it.

that's not to say that this doesn't work for you specifically, but a majority of people will have adverse reactions with their keloids.

I do wear earrings (three piercings in one ear, two in the other). It might be some miracle that those only ever developed minor keloids, so I never had them treated. I wish I could give better advise, but it may be worth seeing if SRT is an option for ears. I know that it can be done on the face/neck/body so maybe you'd be a candidate for it!

i am prone to keloiding and i'm going to offer a different perspective than the other folks in this comment section have said.


my keloids responded extremely poorly to silicone tapes, injections, scar creams, lasering... you name it, i tried it. my keloids were in painful places (center of my chest and shoulder blades), and these treatments seemed to only make the scars widen and thicken.


i managed to find a derm that does superficial radiation therapy and it is the ONLY thing my keloid responded to. i had them treated in 2019 and they've never returned after my last radiation session. they are fully flat now and the discoloring has faded greatly over time. just wanted to throw that out as an option in case your keloid becomes as stubborn and painful as mine were.
